findings.title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before the new FeatureSpec setup that enables rolling-updates. Both parameterized tests (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount) include that null case, which is the documented default strategy. The operator guide in this PR states the preview feature must be enabled or the operator fails, so these cases deploy a CR without the feature and will not exercise (or will fail) the default upgrade path the test is meant to cover. Enable the feature before that return so every strategy, including the default, runs with rolling-updates.

findings.title: Enabling rolling-updates replaces any existing enabled features
findings.body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) overwrites the CR's entire enabled-features list instead of appending. If getTestKeycloakDeployment (or a future caller) already set spec.features.enabled, those features are dropped whenever a non-default UpdateStrategy is applied. The server then starts with a different feature set than the rest of the operator suite, so upgrade assertions can pass or fail for the wrong reason. Add rolling-updates to the existing list rather than replacing it.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test does not assert exit code 4
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error string. This PR makes exit code 4 the contract for a disabled rolling-updates feature (and moves the recreate-upgrade code from 4 to 3). A regression that still prints the message but exits 1, or that leaves recreate on 4, would not be caught. The test should assert exit code 4, and the check subcommand should be covered the same way as metadata.
